Avocado Night Cream vs Avocado Korean Night Cream: Which to Choose

By Mohammed Nihal, founderPublished 20 October 2026Updated 16 October 20266 min read
Quick answer

Both cost ₹649 and contain avocado, aloe vera, vitamin B3 and kojic acid. Choose the 30 g Avocado Night Cream for dry or tight-feeling skin and the best value per gram; choose the 25 g Avocado Korean Night Cream for a smooth, medium texture that suits most skin and humid weather.

  • Avocado Night Cream: 30 g, about ₹21.6 per gram.
  • Avocado Korean Night Cream: 25 g, about ₹26 per gram.
  • Both contain kojic acid, so use one per night, not both.
  • A 30 g jar lasts about 6–8 weeks; 25 g about 5–6 weeks.

Avocado Night Cream vs Avocado Korean Night Cream comes down to texture and size, not ingredients. Both cost ₹649 and both contain avocado, aloe vera, vitamin B3 (niacinamide) and kojic acid. Choose the Avocado Night Cream (30 g) if your skin feels dry or tight and you want the most cream for your money; choose the Avocado Korean Night Cream (25 g) for a smoother, medium texture that suits most skin types and humid weather.

We make both, so this is the plain comparison we give people who ask us on WhatsApp.

What is the same

  • The same four key ingredients. Avocado for softness and nourishment, aloe vera for a light, comfortable feel, vitamin B3 for a smoother, more even-looking tone, and kojic acid to help reduce the look of dark spots over time.
  • The same price, free shipping across India, Cash on Delivery, and 7-day returns on sealed jars.
  • The same rules. Patch test first, start every other night, and wear sunscreen every morning because both contain kojic acid.
  • The same timeline. Skin feels moisturised from the first night; a more even look usually takes 8–12 weeks of regular use.

What is different: texture

This is the real choice. The Avocado Night Cream is richer and more cushioned. It leaves a comforting layer that dry skin drinks up overnight, which is why it suits winter in Delhi or Jaipur, or anyone whose face feels tight after a day in AC.

The Avocado Korean Night Cream is smooth and medium-weight, made in a Korean-inspired style. It spreads easily, sinks in without a heavy film, and sits comfortably under a fan on a humid night in Mumbai, Chennai or Kochi. It suits normal, combination and oily skin, and dry skin in humid months.

Neither is "stronger". They simply feel different on the skin.

What is different: size and value

At the same ₹649, the Avocado Night Cream gives you 5 g more. That works out to about ₹21.6 per gram against about ₹26 per gram, so it is the better value per gram of the two. In practice that is roughly one or two extra weeks of nightly use.

If value is your top priority and your skin is normal to dry, the 30 g jar wins. If the richer texture would feel heavy on you, the extra grams are not worth it, because a cream you dislike wearing does not get used. Our avocado cream price in India guide shows how to compare value fairly, and how long a jar of night cream lasts explains the weeks per jar.

Who should choose which

Choose the Avocado Night Cream if

  • Your skin feels dry, tight or flaky, especially on the cheeks.
  • You live somewhere dry or cold, or spend long hours in air-conditioning.
  • You want the best value per gram for regular nightly use.
  • You are in your 30s or older and your skin wants more cushion at night.

More on this in avocado cream for dry skin.

Choose the Avocado Korean Night Cream if

  • Your skin is normal, combination or oily.
  • You live in a humid or coastal city, or it is summer or monsoon.
  • You prefer a smooth, light-feeling finish under the fan.
  • Your main goal is a softer, more even-looking complexion.

See avocado cream for oily skin for how much to use.

Still not sure?

Pick the Korean one if you are in doubt. A medium texture is easier to adjust: you can add a little more on dry patches. Our skin quiz can also help you decide.

Can you use both?

Yes, but not on the same night. Both contain kojic acid, so layering them doubles the kojic acid without adding anything new, and raises the chance of irritation. Better ways to own both:

  • Switch with the seasons. The Korean cream from roughly March to October, the richer cream in the cooler, drier months.
  • Switch with your setting. The richer one on nights after a long AC day, the Korean one on hot, humid nights.
  • Share between two people in a home with different skin types.

If your skin is sensitive and you want a plain moisturiser on some nights, our Avocado Glow Cream 15 g has avocado and aloe vera only, with no kojic acid.

How to use either one

  1. Patch test behind your ear for 24–48 hours.
  2. At night, cleanse and pat your face dry.
  3. Warm a pea-sized amount between your fingertips and press it over the face and neck.
  4. Use every other night for the first two weeks, then nightly.
  5. Wear SPF 30 or higher every morning.

Full technique in how to apply night cream. Skip both creams for 24–48 hours after waxing, threading or bleach, and see a dermatologist if you have melasma, a rash, or are pregnant.

Shop: Avocado Night Cream, 30 g, ₹649 or Avocado Korean Night Cream, 25 g, ₹649. All our avocado night creams are on the avocado night cream page, and the Korean style is explained on our Korean night cream page.

Short answers

What is the difference between Avocado Night Cream and Avocado Korean Night Cream? The ingredients and price are the same. The Avocado Night Cream is richer and 30 g; the Avocado Korean Night Cream is smoother, medium-weight and 25 g.

Which is better for oily skin? The Avocado Korean Night Cream, used as a thin layer.

Which is better for dry skin? The Avocado Night Cream, especially in winter or AC rooms.

Which is better value? The Avocado Night Cream, at about ₹21.6 per gram against about ₹26 per gram.

Can I use both on the same night? No need. Both contain kojic acid, so use one at a time and switch by season if you like.

This is general skincare information, not medical advice. Patch test any new product, and see a dermatologist if you have a skin condition.
